name: Casio-style phase distortion: piecewise phase warp of a cosine into a saw (DCW node)
goal: Implement Casio CZ-style phase distortion so a cosine (or sine) table becomes a variable saw by warping the 0→1 read phase with a two-slope piecewise line (breakpoint node at half-amplitude), then modulate that node for filter-like brightness without a resonant filter.

source.title: GroovyDSP: Introduction to Phase Distortion Synthesis

prerequisites: Oscillator that can look up a cosine/sine table from an external 0→1 phase (AudioWorklet, modular phase input, or custom DSP)
Oscilloscope to verify phase and output

inputs.name: source_table
inputs.description: Cosine cycle preferred (Casio-style; starts at +1); sine also works with a different starting phase

inputs.name: dcw_node_x
inputs.description: Horizontal position of the breakpoint (x1 in 0..1); smaller = sharper/more saw-like

outputs.name: pd_oscillator
outputs.description: Phase-distortion oscillator with modulatable DCW/brightness node

constraints: Portable signal-flow recipe for Web Audio / Traveler-inspired / any hybrid synth with comparable modules; not affiliated with any vendor.
Do not copy proprietary factory preset banks, wavetable file names, or sample packs; use original/free waves or generic shapes.
Steps and numeric values are grounded only in the YouTube Show-transcript text; approximate where the speaker gestured without stating a number.
Keep each wave cycle the same length regardless of node position (warp the lookup phase; do not change increment speed mid-cycle or pitch drifts).
The piecewise warp introduces a knee/corner that can alias; treat anti-aliasing as a later concern.

steps.action: Treat the oscillator as: play a cosine (or sine) table by reading it with a linear phase ramp 0→1 once per note cycle. At warp=0 the output must equal the untouched cosine.
steps.expect: Scope shows a clean cosine when the phase map is identity (y=x)

steps.action: Define a breakpoint node that always sits at half amplitude on the warped phase (y=0.5) but can slide left on the x-axis to position x1 (how far 'cocked back'). More cock-back = sharper transition from cosine toward saw.
steps.expect: A single control moves the knee while the vertical join stays at mid-cycle amplitude

steps.action: Build the warped phase with two line equations meeting at (x1, 0.5): m1 = 0.5 / x1 for the fast first segment (y = m1 * x); m2 = 0.5 / (1 - x1) and b2 = 1 - m2 for the slow second segment (y = m2 * x + b2). If phase < x1 use the first; else use the second.
steps.expect: Warped phase reaches 0.5 exactly at x1 and 1.0 at the end of the cycle

steps.action: Look up cos(2π * warped_phase) [or your cosine table at warped_phase]. Do not advance phase at two different increments across the threshold — that one missed sample at the knee throws the pitch out of tune when x1 moves.
steps.expect: Pitch stays locked to the note while x1 changes brightness/timbre

steps.action: Listen while moving x1: near 0.5 the tone is closer to a sinusoid; pulled far left toward 0 it approaches a near-pure saw. Route an envelope or LFO to x1 for filter-like sweeps without filter math.
steps.expect: EG/LFO on the node opens/closes brightness like a non-resonant filter

steps.action: Optional extensions (same warper): run the warper twice per cycle for other CZ shapes; feed a rich wave (e.g. square) through the same shaper to get pulse-width/symmetry-style squeezing of the first half vs elongation of the second.
steps.expect: Same phase-warp block serves saw-like PD and PWM-like symmetry duties

verification: With x1≈0.5 output is near-cosine; with x1 near 0 output is near-saw; pitch does not drift as x1 moves
Scope of warped phase shows a two-slope polyline with knee at y=0.5
